finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /settings/email calls set_email with g.uid=None, so an account-changing operation runs without an authenticated user (authorization bypass).
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /settings/email with no session cookie.

trace.note: g.uid = session.get("uid") yields None when no session exists.
change_email runs with no authentication check.
set_email(None, ...) called; hardcoded email, client input ignored.
set_email stub; would persist change keyed by uid.

finding.guards_checked: login_optional only populates g.uid and never rejects (routes.py:19-25); no None check in change_email (routes.py:36-38) or set_email (routes.py:48-49); no CSRF token, rate limit, or re-authentication present in file.

verdict.guard_found: none. login_optional (routes.py:19-25) only sets g.uid = session.get("uid") and never aborts. change_email (routes.py:36-38) has no None check and no login_required. set_email (routes.py:48-49) does no check. No CSRF, rate limit, or re-auth is in this file.
verdict.reason: An anonymous POST to /settings/email (routes.py:34-35) reaches change_email, which calls set_email(None, ...) at routes.py:37 with no authentication check (contrast change_password at routes.py:41-42, which uses login_required). The trace is accurate, but set_email at routes.py:48-49 is a `pass` stub, so the account-changing effect is hypothetical in this file; the finding holds on the route's auth logic, not on observed persistence.

finding.claim: Authenticated POST /settings/password sets the account password to the hardcoded constant "hunter2" with no current-password or re-auth check, enabling persistent account takeover by any session holder and embedding a hardcoded credential.
finding.source: Any holder of a valid session cookie for a user (stolen cookie, unattended session, XSS, or same-site cross-origin POST) sending POST /settings/password.

trace.note: login_required checks only that "uid" is in session.
g.uid set from session without freshness or re-auth check.
set_password writes fixed literal "hunter2" for the uid; no input, no verification.

finding.guards_checked: login_required presence check only (routes.py:8-16); no current-password verification, no re-authentication, no CSRF protection, no password policy in file. Hardcoded literal violates org policy against hardcoded credentials; weakens authentication and must be flagged to Security.

verdict.guard_found: login_required (routes.py:8-16) only checks that "uid" is in the session and aborts with 401 otherwise. Nothing checks a current password, re-authenticates, or verifies a CSRF token. The route at routes.py:41-45 calls set_password(g.uid, "hunter2") unconditionally. The literal "hunter2" is hardcoded at routes.py:44.
verdict.reason: All cited lines match the trace: routes.py:42 applies only the session-presence check in login_required (routes.py:11-13), and routes.py:44 unconditionally calls set_password(g.uid, "hunter2") with a hardcoded literal, so any session holder can reset the account password without knowing the current one. The write itself is in the set_password stub at routes.py:52-53, so the persistent takeover effect depends on an implementation not in this file, but the missing re-authentication and hardcoded credential are verified from the code shown.

finding.claim: Cookie-authenticated state-changing POST routes (/settings/email, /settings/password) have no CSRF token check in this file; protection relies on unverified browser SameSite default.
finding.source: Victim browser with valid session cookie visiting attacker page that auto-submits a cross-site form POST.
finding.sink: set_email at routes.py:37 and set_password at routes.py:44.

trace.note: POST /settings/email accepts requests identified by session cookie.
POST /settings/password accepts requests identified by session cookie.
uid taken from session cookie in login_required.
uid taken from session cookie in login_optional.

finding.guards_checked: No CSRF token validation in file; SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE not set in file, so protection depends on browser default (typically Lax) and deployment config not visible here.

verdict.guard_found: No in-code CSRF control. routes.py has no token check, no SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE setting, and the repo-wide grep for samesite/csrf/SESSION_COOKIE finds no implementation (only skill docs). The only candidate mitigation is the browser's default SameSite handling, which is outside the code. Flask's default leaves SameSite unset (routes.py:3-5 shows no config).
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (routes.py:13, 22, 34, 37, 41, 42-44 match the claims), and nothing in the code blocks a cross-site POST to /settings/email (routes.py:34-38) or /settings/password (routes.py:41-45). Whether that POST carries the victim's session cookie depends on the browser's default SameSite behavior and deployment config, neither of which is visible here, so the finding cannot be confirmed or refuted from this code alone.
